outputs.headline: False: 5G mobile towers do not spread coronavirus
outputs.summary: The claim that 5G mobile towers spread the coronavirus is false; scientific and health organizations confirm viruses cannot travel on radio waves.
outputs.what_post_claims: The post claims that 5G mobile towers spread the coronavirus, causing an increase in cases where 5G was installed.
outputs.what_is_true: Scientific and health organizations worldwide have confirmed that 5G technology cannot spread viruses. COVID-19 is a respiratory illness spread through droplets from an infected person, and viruses cannot travel on radio waves or mobile networks.
evidence_against: NIH.gov states that the claim about 5G spreading coronavirus is a debunked conspiracy theory.
UN News reported that the International Telecommunications Union (ITU) called the 5G-COVID-19 theory a hoax with no technical basis.
The Washington Post reported that experts confirm it is physically impossible for electromagnetic fields to transfer viruses.
outputs.sources_spoken: according to NIH.gov, UN News, and The Washington Post
outputs.audio_script: The post claims that 5G mobile towers spread the coronavirus, leading to more cases where 5G was installed. This is false. Scientific and health organizations worldwide confirm that 5G technology cannot spread viruses. COVID-19 is a respiratory illness spread through droplets from an infected person, and viruses cannot travel on radio waves or mobile networks. We are very sure of this. This information comes from sources like NIH.gov, UN News, and The Washington Post.
card_lines: Truth: Viruses cannot travel on radio waves
